title: REALM: Learning to Retrieve Before You Pre-Train

beats.text: Forcing models to cram all world knowledge into raw network weights is an absolute computational nightmare.
beats.visual_focus: A massive neural network mesh expanding uncontrollably as text facts overload each individual floating-point weight.

visual_blueprint.title: PARAMETRIC OVERLOAD
visual_blueprint.sub: Dense networks forced to memorize factual corpora

motif_params.title: PARAMETRIC OVERLOAD
motif_params.sub: Dense networks forced to memorize factual corpora

beats.text: Dense transformers act like students forced to memorize an entire library. Scaling model weights just to recall trivial facts burns massive GPU memory.
beats.visual_focus: A GPU core surrounded by gigabytes of static VRAM weights holding trivia strings, stalled while querying internal parameters.

visual_blueprint.title: THE MEMORY WALL
visual_blueprint.sub: Implicit knowledge storage bloating network capacity

motif_params.title: THE MEMORY WALL
motif_params.sub: Implicit knowledge storage bloating network capacity

beats.text: Enter REALM. Instead of brute-force memorization. It gives the transformer an external knowledge retriever before it ever begins pre-training.
beats.visual_focus: The transformer core detaching from static memory and linking via high-speed vector rays to an external Wikipedia document bank.

beats.text: It routes queries through an indexed Wikipedia corpus. Backpropagating masked language modeling loss straight through the document retrieval step.
beats.visual_focus: Chalkboard schematic showing gradient arrows traveling backwards from masked text tokens straight through document search probabilities into the retriever.

visual_blueprint.title: CENTRAL INDEX DISPATCH: GRADIENTS

beats.text: On Open-QA benchmarks. REALM beats dense baselines by up to sixteen percent absolute accuracy. With transparent modularity and instant document updates.
